description: Blind A/B routing corpus for the semantic-first experiment. Two segments: (1) international/paraphrase cases that express the SAME intents as routing-benchmark.json but in plain non-native English avoiding the trigger keywords the deterministic pre-router matches on; (2) a sample drawn from routing-benchmark.json spanning all tiers including false-positive guards. Combined the corpus measures whether reading-for-intent-first (Arm B) recovers the long tail of paraphrased requests without regressing the safety-critical force-routes (pr-workflow, security-review) or re-introducing false positives. Each paraphrase case avoids the exact trigger phrases listed in skills/INDEX.json so pre-route.py falls through and the semantic router is the only path that can recover the route. Extension (v1.1, feat/route-ab-harness): 50 additional cases in five new buckets — stub-tier (skills with zero recorded routes; tiered-manifest tripwire), sibling-disambiguation, pipeline-pick (optional expected_pipeline; near-misses must return pipeline null), vague-interview (underspecified requests that should land planning), and plain-english (non-jargon phrasing). Optional fields: expected_pipeline (default null), acceptable (list of {agent, skill} alternates), uncertain (best-effort gold label). Absence of the optional fields means legacy behavior; the 49 legacy cases are byte-identical to v1.0. Extension (v1.2, feat/full-catalog-reachability): 73 reachability cases covering every previously-uncovered routable skill in the merged catalog. Bucket "reachability" — held-out probes expressing genuine user needs without quoting trigger keywords. 22 skills classified never-routable-by-design (voice profiles, shared patterns, pipeline sub-skills, internal orchestration). Extension (v1.3, feat/aggressive-routing-wave1): 91 cases drawn from 128 recorded production dispatches that fell back to general-purpose. The corpus before this extension asserted expected_agent null on 142 of 178 cases (79.8%), so a router that routed LESS scored BETTER and under-routing was undetectable. Four new buckets: prod-fallback-specialist (a domain agent is correct), prod-fallback-general (general-purpose is correct, labelled explicitly rather than null so over-routing also fails), prod-fallback-coordinator (multi-deliverable conjunctive requests; project-coordinator-engineer was chosen zero times in 287 dispatches), and prod-fallback-ambiguous (expected_agent null WITH a stated reason). expected_agent may now be the built-in agent name general-purpose, which is absent from agents/INDEX.json by design; routing-benchmark.py accepts built-in agent names, matching validate-do-references.py and validate-merged-index.py. The requests come from one Flask/Peewee/SQLite site plus its ops surface, so `acceptable` sometimes names five-star-booker, that repo's project skill, which lives in the local overlay index rather than the public one. Extension (v1.4, feat/aggressive-routing-wave1): every taggable case carries `provenance` {source, workload, sample}. This toolkit runs on several machines with different workloads, and learning.db is per-box with no host or project column and no cross-box aggregation — so a local sample is evidence about ONE machine and local absence is NOT evidence that an agent or skill is unused anywhere. source is one of: local-telemetry (recorded dispatches from a single machine; workload names it), catalog-derived (written from INDEX semantics, no telemetry), unknown-legacy (provenance not recorded at the time). The 49 pinned v1.0 cases cannot carry the field without breaking their SHA-256 pin, so ABSENCE resolves to unknown-legacy; they are believed to be paraphrases of routing-benchmark.json, but that is not recorded, so it is not asserted. test_no_single_workload_dominates_agent_labels caps any one workload's share of the agent-asserting cases: without it, a corpus tuned to one box could certify a routing change that regresses every other box — the #860 failure mode pointed the other way.
